{{nihongo|'''Tsubaki Grand Shrine'''|椿大神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Suzuka, Mie|Q207311|qid=Q207311}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}. {{nihongo|'''Tsubaki Grand Shrine'''|椿大神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ise Province]].

== Overview ==
It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} and the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Ise Province|Q864166|qid=Q864166}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine rank system}} it was a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}, and today it is a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}. In Mie Prefecture it ranks third in number of worshipers after {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}} and {{ill|Futami Okitama Shrine|Q64969614|qid=Q64969614}}; in 2013 it had 1,455,000 visitors<ref>{{Cite web|和書|publisher=Mie Prefecture Employment and Economy Dept., Tourism and International Bureau, Tourism Policy Division|url=http://www.pref.mie.lg.jp/TOPICS/201405010921.pdf|title=Visitor counts by tourism site category|accessdate=2015-01-25|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150124151905/http://www.pref.mie.lg.jp/TOPICS/201405010921.pdf|archivedate=2015-01-24}}</ref>.

It is also called '''Sarutahiko Daihongu''', and is regarded as the head shrine of shrines enshrining Sarutahiko Ōkami.

== Enshrined deities ==
; Main enshrined deity
* '''{{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami}}'''

; Co-enshrined deities
* {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Takuhadachiji-hime|Q11110848|qid=Q11110848}} - mother deity of Ninigi-no-Mikoto

; Associated deities
* {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|Q462803|qid=Q462803|lt=Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto}} - consort deity of Sarutahiko Ōkami
* {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto}}

; Forward seat
* Gyoman Daimyojin

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, in the 27th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850}}, by an oracle to {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}}, a shrine building was constructed near the tomb of Sarutahiko Ōkami as "the shrine of Michiwake Ōkami." The first historical appearance is in the June 17, {{ill|748|Q23621|qid=Q23621}} ({{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} 20) ''Daian-ji Garan Engi narabi ni Ryuki Shizaicho''. This shrine is generally identified with "Tsubaki Ōkamiyashiro" in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}'' and as the ichinomiya of Ise Province.

Tradition says Gyoman Daimyojin, a descendant of Sarutahiko Ōkami, founded {{ill|Shugendō|Q1483875|qid=Q1483875}} and guided {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=En no Gyoja}}, and the shrine became a center of shugendo-shinto in the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}. The current priests are said to descend from Gyoman Daimyojin.

In {{ill|1871|ab|1871|af|1871|als|1871|am|1871 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1871|ar|1871|ary|1871|arz|1871|ast|1871|av|1871 сон|avk|1871|az|1871|azb|۱۸۷۱ (میلادی)|ba|1871 йыл|ban|1871|bar|1871|bat_smg|1871|bcl|1871|be|1871|be_x_old|1871|bg|1871|bn|১৮৭১|bpy|মারি ১৮৭১|br|1871|bs|1871.|ca|1871|cdo|1871 nièng|ce|1871 шо|ceb|1871|ckb|١٨٧١|crh|1871|cs|1871|csb|1871|cv|1871|cy|1871|da|1871|de|1871|diq|1871|el|1871|eml|1871|eo|1871|es|1871|et|1871|eu|1871|fa|۱۸۷۱|fi|1871|fiu_vro|1871|fo|1871|fr|1871|frp|1871|frr|1871|fur|1871|fy|1871|ga|1871|gan|1871年|gcr|1871|gd|1871|gl|1871|gv|1871|hak|1871-ngièn|he|1871|hi|१८७१|hif|1871|hr|1871.|hsb|1871|ht|1871 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1871|hy|1871|hyw|1871 թուական|ia|1871|id|1871|ilo|1871|io|1871|is|1871|it|1871|ja|1871年|jv|1871|ka|1871|kaa|1871|kk|1871 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೧|ko|1871년|krc|1871 джыл|ku|1871|kv|1871-ӧд во|kw|1871|la|1871|lb|1871|lez|1871 йис|li|1871|lij|1871|lmo|1871|lt|1871 m.|lv|1871. gads|mai|१८७१|map_bms|1871|mdf|1871|mg|1871|mhr|1871|mi|1871|min|1871|mk|1871|mr|इ.स. १८७१|mrj|1871 и|ms|1871|my|၁၈၇၁|myv|1871 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۱|nah|1871|nap|1871|nds|1871|new|ई सं १८७१|nl|1871|nn|1871|no|1871|nrm|1871|nso|1871|oc|1871|olo|1871|or|୧୮୭୧|os|1871-æм аз|pa|1871|pap|1871|pl|1871|pnb|1871|pt|1871|qu|1871|ro|1871|ru|1871 год|rue|1871|sa|१८७१|sah|1871|sc|1871|scn|1871|sd|1871ع|se|1871|sh|1871.|shn|1871|si|1871|simple|1871|sk|1871|sl|1871|smn|1871|sq|1871|sr|1871|stq|1871|su|1871|sv|1871|sw|1871|szl|1871|ta|1871|te|1871|tg|Соли 1871|th|พ.ศ. 2414|tk|1871|tl|1871|tly|1871|tr|1871|tt|1871 ел|udm|1871 ар|ug|1871 - يىلى|uk|1871|ur|1871ء|uz|1871|vec|1871|vi|1871|vls|1871|vo|1871|wa|1871|war|1871|wuu|1871年|xmf|1871|yi|1871|za|1871 nienz|zea|1871|zh|1871年|zh_classical|一八七一年|zh_min_nan|1871 nî|zh_yue|1871年|qid=Q7746}} (Meiji 4), it was listed as gosha under the modern ranking system, and in {{ill|1927|Q18110|qid=Q18110}} (Showa 2) it became kensha. In {{ill|1935|Q18658|qid=Q18658}} (Showa 10), a survey by the Interior Ministry's Shrine Bureau designated it the head shrine ("Chigi Sarutahiko Daihongu") for about 2,000 Sarutahiko shrines nationwide. In practice, only a small number of those shrines have direct ties with this shrine. Meanwhile, shrines called "{{ill|Tsubaki Shrine (disambiguation)|Q11541039|qid=Q11541039}}" enshrining "Tsubaki Daimyojin" exist in many regions.

In {{ill|1987|Q2429|qid=Q2429}} (Showa 62), it founded Tsubaki America Shrine (now {{ill|Tsubaki Grand Shrine of America|Q840967|qid=Q840967}} in Washington State), beginning active promotion of {{ill|Shinto|Q812767|qid=Q812767}} in the United States.

Its treasures include a lion head said to have been dedicated by {{ill|Kibi no Makibi|Q1063276|qid=Q1063276}}, and the shrine is also considered a birthplace shrine of {{ill|Lion dance|Q713866|qid=Q713866}} lion dance.

== Subsidiary shrines ==
== Betsugu ==
[[画像:Uzume-honguu shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Betsugu: Tsubakigishi Shrine]]

* '''Tsubakigishi Shrine''' - deities: Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto, Futodama-no-Mikoto, Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto
* Okunomiya Iwaza (summit of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nyudogatake}}) - deities: Amaterasu, Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Sarutahiko Ōkami
* Ogishi Ōkami Shrine (Kogisu-cho, Suzuka) - deities: Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto, Takamimusubi-no-kami
* Aishoi Shrine (Mizusawa-Noda-cho, Yokkaichi) - deity: Aishoi Daigongen
* Ishi Ōkami (Kogisu-cho, Suzuka) - deity: Amaterasu

== Festivals ==
* Shishi Shin-go Kito ritual: Feb 11 - Apr 12 (once every 3 years)
** In years of Ox, Dragon, Sheep, and Dog
** First dance on Feb 11; concluding dance in precinct on Apr 12
* Setsubun Festival: day of Setsubun in February
* Kinen-sai / Great purification festival: Feb 21
* Spring annual grand festival
** Spring grand festival: Apr 11 (dedication of Kyoto {{ill|Kongō-ryū|Q11646539|qid=Q11646539}} ritual nō "Uzume")
** Kōsha grand festival: Apr 11-12
* Koryujin Shrine grand festival: early May
* Nyudogatake summit Okunomiya spring grand festival: May 12
* Rice-planting festival: last Sunday of May
* Summer purification: Jun 30
* Summer festival: Aug 1
* Autumn annual grand festival
** Eve festival: Oct 10
** Main shrine grand festival: Oct 11
** Betsugu grand festival: Oct 12
* Nyudogatake summit Okunomiya autumn grand festival: Nov 12
* Niiname Festival: Dec 1
* New Year's Eve great purification: Dec 31

== Access ==
=== Bus ===
* From {{ill|Kintetsu Yokkaichi Station|Q6414379|qid=Q6414379|lt=Kintetsu Yokkaichi Station}} / {{ill|Yokkaichi Station|Q5358995|qid=Q5358995|lt=JR Yokkaichi Station}}, take {{ill|Mie Kotsu|Q6843516|qid=Q6843516}} bus (bound for Tsubaki Grand Shrine), get off at final stop.
* From Kintetsu {{ill|Hiratachō Station|Q5769516|qid=Q5769516}} / JR {{ill|Kasado Station|Q5358774|qid=Q5358774}}, take Suzuka community bus (C-BUS, Tsubaki-Hirata line loop), get off at "Tsubaki Ōkamiyashiro" stop.

=== Private car ===
* About 5 km from {{ill|Suzuka interchange|Q11649468|qid=Q11649468}} on the {{ill|Higashi-Meihan Expressway|Q5753692|qid=Q5753692}}
* (ETC vehicles only) about 2 km from {{ill|Suzuka parking area|Q11649477|qid=Q11649477}} on the {{ill|Shin-Meishin Expressway|Q7497118|qid=Q7497118}}
